# Flyology JSON

> Experimental Ada-first incremental JSON parser and transactional streaming writer.

Flyology JSON 0.1.0-dev is not yet released in the Flyology Alire index. The bounded core performs no heap allocation. Callers supply input, event storage, duplicate-name storage, token storage, and writer destination staging.

## Documentation

- [Overview](https://json.flyology.org/): project boundary and design summary
- [Guide](https://json.flyology.org/guide/): task-oriented entry points
- [Getting started](https://json.flyology.org/guide/getting-started/): build and run the maintained examples
- [Incremental parsing](https://json.flyology.org/guide/parsing/): Step, Drain, events, raw ranges, and lifecycle
- [Transactional writing](https://json.flyology.org/guide/writing/): destination contract, grammar calls, and publication
- [Tokens and numbers](https://json.flyology.org/guide/tokens-and-numbers/): bounded collection and checked signed or unsigned integer conversion
- [Profiles and errors](https://json.flyology.org/guide/profiles-and-errors/): explicit acceptance policy and coordinates
- [Architecture](https://json.flyology.org/architecture/): ownership and transaction boundaries
- [Support](https://json.flyology.org/support/): current evidence and limitations
- [API reference](https://json.flyology.org/api/): generated GNATdoc reference

## Current boundary

- Parser events are provisional until Document_Complete.
- Exact number lexemes remain octets; checked signed and unsigned integer conversion is separate.
- Reject_Duplicates compares decoded names without Unicode normalization. Preserve_Unchecked emits every name and does not select a winner.
- Ordinary_Compact writer output is deterministic for the same call sequence, but it is not canonical JSON.
- Binary64, decimal, accounting, canonical output, a DOM, and Type IR adapters are future work.
- Flyology Wire does not depend on this crate.
